text: Gladius, the Beast of Night, is one being who welcomed the touch of the Night rather than fearing it.
During the fight with Heolstor, he appears restrained, with a dagger and a greatsword thrust into him and bound by a chanted incantation, implying prior conflict with him.

Gladius represents the principle of pure martial force and conflict without resolution, reducing all interaction to combat with no other mode of behavior; fighting against Gladius's influence only strengthened it, since resistance fed the force itself.

Libra represents the principle of absolute, objective judgment taken to a catastrophic extreme, lacking context, intention, and mercy, turning Limveld's courts and religious authorities into instruments of rigid verdict lacking flexibility.

Maris represents the oldest cosmological force among the Night Lords, associated with ancient forces from the sea and depths that had been contained since before the Golden Order's dominance, which began pressing into inland and underground spaces.

Equilibrian represents the principle of opposing forces locked in permanent, irresolvable stasis resulting from two equally matched forces that cannot yield to each other, turning political and personal conflicts in Limveld into irreconcilable standoffs.
The Night Lord encountered at the end of the third night is the full manifestation of the force that shaped the entire expedition, not just a powerful enemy.
Gladius is characterized by constant motion, and areas most influenced by it show signs of ongoing conflict even outside direct combat, including unaffiliated creatures fighting each other.
Libra's areas of influence are marked by stillness, conveying a sense of suspended judgment awaiting a verdict.
Each Night Lord's combat encounter takes place in an environment that reflects and amplifies its specific principle.
Item descriptions and environmental evidence suggest Gladius was once a warrior whose martial excellence served a purpose beyond combat itself, before becoming what it is now.
Balancer and Dreglord are the two Night Lords introduced in the Forsaken Hollows DLC.
Balancer represents a cosmic ledger of accumulated debts that existence maintains and eventually calls due.
Dreglord represents the accumulation of everything discarded, dismissed, or declared insufficient by civilizations and cosmic processes.
The leader of the Night is called the Night Lord, described by the Priestess as a 'living cataclysm.'
The first Night Lord fought by the Nightfarers is Gladius, a wolf born uniquely with three heads.
The second Night Lord is Adel, a dragon that was once the apex predator of its region.
The third Night Lord, Noster, is composed of two insects resembling a white satin moth and a scorpion.
In the boss fight, Noster's moth and scorpion work together and eventually merge partway through the battle.
Noster's moth has a grab attack that leaves behind a poisoning parasite, hinting it may exploit its scorpion partner as well.
The fourth Night Lord is known as Augur, battled under the name Maris, Fathom of Night.
Maris's lore describes it as an unknown entity that drifted through the skies, blending with its surroundings as if in a dream.
The fifth Night Lord is Libra, called the Demon of Night, a goat-headed being disguised as a man who practices dubious alchemy.
The sixth Night Lord is Fulgor, titled Champion of Nightglow, an ancient centaur consumed by battle fervor who wields a sacred form of the Night's power.
In exchange for his loss, the Night gifted Fulgor a new left arm.
The seventh Night Lord is Caligo, Miasma of Night, a prehistoric dragon that watched the world from atop a fog-shrouded mountain.
Fulgor, despite serving the Night, uses Holy-aligned attacks, a contradiction that remains unexplained.
The final boss is Heolstor, the Night Lord, who first appears as the Shape of Night before his true name is revealed.
Heolstor's description states that beyond the boundless night lies the hazy figure of a person, called the Night's origin and an enemy to the world.
Heolstor is called the primordial Night Lord, implying he is the very first Night Lord to exist.
After his defeat, Heolstor tears open a hole in the fabric of time.
During the Shape of Night phase, cloth bearing golden scripture, similar to the Cipher Pata weapon, appears to restrain the black essence within Heolstor before bursting free after a killing blow.
Heolstor's body is hollow, containing only black essence and a Great Rune, reminiscent of how Radagon's body was incomplete in Elden Ring.
Margit and Godrick appear as bosses in Nightreign under the names Fell Omen and Grafted Monarch, respectively.
Fell Omen (Margit) can be fought during the game's intro, assumed to be unwinnable at first, but can be rematched through the Visual Codex.
Grafted Monarch (Godrick) wields his axe and a dragon head in a second phase but has gained new Crucible powers not present in Elden Ring.
